narrativeReportMd:
# MedicationDispense R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
The R6 artifact exists with the same canonical identity, but local content-model changes create high-impact breaking changes. The most important are `medication[x]` moving to required `CodeableReference`, `subject` becoming mandatory, required status code `stopped` becoming `unfulfilled`, `dosageInstruction` changing from repeating `Dosage` to singleton `DosageDetails`, removal of `detectedIssue`, and `context` narrowing to `encounter`.

## Scope
This report covers local MedicationDispense changes only and excludes inherited base-artifact changes.

## Main migration themes
Migration requires structural transforms, terminology mapping, and explicit data-preservation policy for removed/narrowed fields. R6-to-R4 conversion also needs extension or data-loss strategies for widened reference targets, multiple categories, and new optional fields.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact findings are the required medication representation change, mandatory subject, status terminology rename, and dosageInstruction type/cardinality replacement.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is important for missing subjects, EpisodeOfCare context, detected issues, complex dosage instructions, multiple substitution responsible parties, and R6 down-conversion of category/new-element content.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes are probably justified by clearer modeling, but aliases, deprecation, or profile-level requirements could have reduced some breaks.

## Follow-up analysis
Datatype-level CodeableReference/DosageDetails reports and terminology ConceptMaps would improve conversion guidance.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: MedicationDispense has high-impact local R4→R6 breaks despite unchanged resource identity. Main concerns are required medication serialization, mandatory subject, status code rename, dosage/type cardinality replacement, and removed/narrowed clinical context fields. Confidence is high for structural facts and medium for rationale.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Use explicit converters: choice-to-CodeableReference wrapping, subject backfill policy, status ConceptMap, dosage conversion, removed-field preservation, and R6-to-R4 extension strategy for new/widened content.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high because the local R4/R6 StructureDefinitions and relevant local CodeSystems/ValueSets were inspected. Confidence is limited for intent and ideal migration policy because official diffs, live terminology expansions, narrative pages, and ConceptMaps were not available.

findings.title: Required medication choice element was replaced by required CodeableReference

newState.summary: R6 requires non-choice `medication` of type CodeableReference targeting Medication.

semanticText.short: What medication was (or was intended to be) supplied

impact.impactRationaleMd: Mandatory element wire shape changed. R4 instances have an old choice-name property and no R6 `medication`; R6 CodeableReference can also contain both concept and reference, which R4 choice syntax cannot represent.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adopting `CodeableReference` for medication identity is a coherent R6 modeling goal because it normalizes coded and referenced medication identity in one container. A less-breaking design exists, but it would leave overlapping same-resource representations for a required, safety-relevant fact, so the breaking design is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative could keep the R4 `medication[x]` choice valid, possibly deprecated, and add a new CodeableReference path for R6 content. That would preserve existing R4 wire format for code-only and reference-only instances, but systems would need precedence and consistency rules if old and new medication fields were both populated, and the old choice form cannot natively preserve a single item that carries both a concept and a reference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain R4 `medication[x]` as deprecated while adding or preferring an R6 CodeableReference representation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves code-only and reference-only R4 instances, but creates duplicate mandatory medication identity paths and needs rules for paired concept/reference values.

evidence.detail: R4 type is CodeableConcept or Reference(Medication), min 1.
CodeableReference has separate concept and reference children.

findings.narrativeMd: `medication[x]` changed to `medication` CodeableReference. Because the element is required, every raw R4 instance needs a structural transform before R6 validation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old `medicationCodeableConcept`/`medicationReference` properties are invalid in R6. Reverse conversion is straightforward only when R6 has exactly one of concept or reference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 code to `medication.concept` and R4 reference to `medication.reference`; define a down-conversion policy for dual-populated CodeableReference; update generated model accessors and tests.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A compatibility alias or deprecation period could have reduced disruption, but would duplicate medication representation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 required medication used the choice properties `medicationCodeableConcept` or `medicationReference`; R6 requires a single `medication` CodeableReference. That is a real wire-format and generated-model break for a central, required clinical fact, and an R6 CodeableReference with both concept and reference cannot round-trip cleanly to the R4 choice. Even so, the R6 modeling goal is coherent: one element can carry either coded or referenced medication identity. Keeping the old choice properties as base aliases would duplicate the required medication representation and create conflict and precedence rules for safety-relevant data.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot element `MedicationDispense.medication[x]`: min 1, max 1, CodeableConcept or Reference(Medication).
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot element `MedicationDispense.medication`: min 1, max 1, CodeableReference(Medication).
R6 CodeableReference defines separate optional `concept` and `reference` children.
freshReview.fmmEffect: MedicationDispense is supplied as R4 FMM 2 / trial-use, so maturity is neutral; the concern comes from required medication identity and safety relevance, not from a heightened stability promise.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old R4 choice JSON properties are not the R6 element; runtime/API/codegen accessors also change, with additional R6-to-R4 loss when both CodeableReference children are populated.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial less-breaking base design could retain deprecated `medication[x]` while adding CodeableReference, preserving many R4 instances. The tradeoff is substantial duplicate same-resource medication identity and difficult consistency rules, and it still would not represent a dual concept/reference CodeableReference in R4.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing high-impact assessment and partial alternative judgment; the break is real but proportionate to the R6 design goal.

findings.title: MedicationDispense.subject became mandatory

impact.impactRationaleMd: A min cardinality increase from 0 to 1 directly invalidates R4 instances that omitted subject.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Subject is patient/group context; unsafe inference can create clinical and privacy errors.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure every dispense identifies its recipient.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of ensuring a patient or group recipient is clinically and operationally strong, especially for safety, privacy, and attribution. A profile-level or warning-based alternative would avoid invalidating old records, but it would not deliver the same base-resource guarantee, so the break is probably justified despite the migration burden.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial less-breaking design would retain `subject` at `0..1` in the base resource and make recipient presence mandatory only in profiles or best-practice rules. That protects old partial or historical records, but base R6 consumers could no longer assume a dispense has recipient context, and unsafe inference of missing subjects would remain a migration risk.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep base `subject` optional and require or warn on it through profiles, best-practice guidance, or jurisdictional rules.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves historical records with no subject, but weakens the base guarantee that every dispense identifies its recipient.

findings.narrativeMd: `subject` is now mandatory. Historical or partial R4 dispense records without a subject become invalid.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid when `subject` is absent; R6-to-R4 is not a problem because R4 can carry the element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory missing-subject records and populate only from authoritative order, encounter, or dispensing context; otherwise quarantine or flag for review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Base requiredness could have been profile-level, but the R6 base requirement gives stronger recipient-context guarantees.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `MedicationDispense.subject` moved from optional to required. Any historical R4 dispense without a subject is old-valid/new-invalid in R6, and backfilling a patient or group can be unsafe if it is inferred from weak context. However, recipient identity is fundamental to a dispense for clinical safety, privacy, and attribution, so a base requirement is a plausible R6 goal. Softer approaches would preserve partial records but would not give R6 consumers the same guarantee.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot element `MedicationDispense.subject`: min 0, max 1, Reference(Patient|Group).
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot element `MedicationDispense.subject`: min 1, max 1, same reference targets.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 / trial-use is neutral. It does not demand normative stability, but it also does not discount a required recipient-context break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances omitting `subject` fail the R6 minimum cardinality.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could keep base `subject` optional and require it through profiles, warnings, or jurisdictional rules. That preserves incomplete records but fails the core base-resource goal that every R6 dispense identifies the recipient.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing high-impact assessment and partial alternative judgment; the base break is justified by the recipient-context guarantee.

findings.title: Required status binding replaced `stopped` with `unfulfilled` and changed CodeSystem canonical

oldState.summary: R4 required status value set includes `stopped`.

newState.summary: R6 required status value set includes `unfulfilled` instead of `stopped` and uses `http://hl7.org/fhir/CodeSystem/medicationdispense-status`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Required binding makes `stopped` invalid in R6 and `unfulfilled` invalid in R4. Enum code, status switches, terminology caches, and modifier-status logic need an explicit map.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify lifecycle terminology and move the code system canonical.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of clearer lifecycle wording is reasonable, but the local definitions for R4 `stopped` and R6 `unfulfilled` are effectively the same. Because this is a required modifier binding, removing the old code creates validation, enum, and workflow breaks that a deprecated-code alias could have avoided with modest long-term terminology cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 base design could include both `stopped` and `unfulfilled` in the required value set, mark `stopped` as legacy or deprecated, and publish a ConceptMap from `stopped` to `unfulfilled`. That preserves R4-valid instances while allowing new R6 systems to prefer the clearer term; the main tradeoff is carrying a legacy synonym that terminology servers and generated enums must continue to recognize.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `stopped` as a deprecated legacy code while adding `unfulfilled` and an explicit ConceptMap.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds synonym/deprecation handling to a required value set, but avoids invalidating existing modifier-status values.

evidence.detail: R6 includes unfulfilled and no stopped.

findings.narrativeMd: `status` is still required and modifier, but one lifecycle code was renamed. This is a hard terminology break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Strict validators reject the old or new code depending on version. The CodeSystem canonical also changed behind the value set.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `stopped` ↔ `unfulfilled`, update generated enums and workflow rules, and test all statuses. Prefer an official ConceptMap if available.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping a deprecated alias would have reduced validation breaks at the cost of carrying legacy vocabulary.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The required modifier `status` binding replaces R4 `stopped` with R6 `unfulfilled` while the local definitions describe the same state: actions implied by the dispense have been permanently halted before all occurred. Strict validators, generated enums, switch statements, and status-driven workflows can reject old or new instances depending on version. Because the semantic change appears to be a rename in a required modifier code, a deprecated-code alias looks like a relatively low-cost way to preserve old instances.
keyEvidence: R4 `MedicationDispense.status` has required binding to `medicationdispense-status|4.0.1` and includes code `stopped`.
R6 `MedicationDispense.status` has required binding to `medicationdispense-status|6.0.0-ballot4` and includes `unfulfilled` instead of `stopped`.
Local R4 `stopped` and R6 `unfulfilled` CodeSystem definitions are materially the same.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 / trial-use is neutral, but required modifier status is central enough that avoidable terminology churn still deserves scrutiny.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: required binding rejects `stopped` in R6; R6-to-R4 loss also occurs because `unfulfilled` is not an R4 code.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could include both codes in R6, mark `stopped` as deprecated or legacy, and publish a ConceptMap to `unfulfilled`. The tradeoff is carrying a synonym in terminology and generated enums, but that cost is modest compared with invalidating a required modifier value.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing high-impact and less-breaking-alternative assessment; this is a good candidate for standards revisit.

findings.title: statusReason[x] was renamed to notPerformedReason and converted to CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 optional `statusReason[x]` was CodeableConcept or Reference(DetectedIssue).

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using the optional old choice names are invalid in R6; R6 can hold both concept and reference, while R4 can hold only one choice.

justification.inferredGoal: Use clearer non-performance naming and CodeableReference.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goals of clearer non-performance naming and `CodeableReference` normalization are reasonable. Keeping the R4 choice names would reduce wire breakage, but it would leave duplicate paths for the same reason and still would not cleanly represent a paired concept and DetectedIssue reference in the old choice shape.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative could keep `statusReasonCodeableConcept` and `statusReasonReference` as deprecated aliases while introducing `notPerformedReason`. That would preserve R4 instances that use this optional element, but R6 validators and applications would need mutual-exclusion, precedence, or equivalence rules when both old and new forms appear, and old clients could not represent a single CodeableReference with both children.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `statusReason[x]` compatibility aliases while adding `notPerformedReason` CodeableReference.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves optional old reason fields, but duplicates non-performance reason semantics and needs conflict rules.

findings.narrativeMd: The optional reason for non-performance changed name and wrapper datatype.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old choice property names are not R6 elements; reverse conversion of dual concept/reference is policy-dependent.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map CodeableConcept to `notPerformedReason.concept` and Reference to `.reference`; update FHIRPath/codegen references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The semantic cleanup is useful but could have been staged with a deprecated alias.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 optional `statusReason[x]` became R6 optional `notPerformedReason` using CodeableReference. R4 payloads using `statusReasonCodeableConcept` or `statusReasonReference` need a structural rename/wrap, and generated models or FHIRPath expressions against the old choice break. The affected element is optional and the R6 name better matches the existing definition that this is why a dispense was not performed. Deprecated aliases would reduce migration friction but would duplicate the same non-performance reason surface.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot element `MedicationDispense.statusReason[x]`: max 1, CodeableConcept or Reference(DetectedIssue), example binding.
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot element `MedicationDispense.notPerformedReason`: max 1, CodeableReference(DetectedIssue), example binding.
Both R4 and R6 definitions describe the reason why a dispense was not performed.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 / trial-use is neutral. The optionality of this path lowers blast radius, while non-performance rationale keeps it clinically meaningful when present.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old choice property names are not R6 elements; runtime/API/codegen paths change, and R6-to-R4 loss is possible for a CodeableReference with both concept and reference.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial alternative could keep deprecated `statusReason[x]` aliases while adding `notPerformedReason`. That would preserve many old instances but create duplicate reason fields, conflict rules, and incomplete support for dual CodeableReference content.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing medium-impact and partial-alternative assessment; the migration burden is real but proportionate.

findings.title: context was renamed to encounter and EpisodeOfCare target was removed

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old `context` name is absent in R6. Encounter context can be renamed; EpisodeOfCare context has no direct R6 base target.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying this relationship as an encounter-specific link is a reasonable R6 cleanup, and the target removal is a real semantic narrowing. A compatibility field could preserve old instances, but it would only partially meet the R6 goal because consumers would have to reconcile `context` and `encounter`, and EpisodeOfCare context semantics could persist indefinitely.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial less-breaking design could retain `context` as a deprecated compatibility element with Encounter and EpisodeOfCare targets, while directing new R6 content to `encounter` and using a separate element or extension if EpisodeOfCare remains important. This preserves R4 data but creates overlapping Encounter carriers and leaves broad contextual references in a resource that R6 appears to be narrowing to encounter context.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `context` for R4 Encounter/EpisodeOfCare references while adding or preferring `encounter`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old context data, but keeps broad EpisodeOfCare/context semantics alongside the narrower encounter-specific path.

findings.narrativeMd: `context` became `encounter`; EpisodeOfCare is no longer valid in the local element.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `context` is invalid as an R6 property. EpisodeOfCare references cannot be mechanically renamed.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename Encounter references to `encounter`; preserve EpisodeOfCare via extension, supporting linkage, or profile-specific policy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A less-breaking approach could have kept `context` deprecated or retained EpisodeOfCare separately.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `context` could reference Encounter or EpisodeOfCare; R6 replaces it with `encounter` and only allows Encounter. Encounter-valued R4 data can be renamed, but EpisodeOfCare context has no direct base R6 slot and needs an extension, external linkage, or policy decision. The encounter-specific cleanup is plausible, but the combined wire-name break and target removal looks more disruptive than necessary if episode-level context remains clinically or administratively meaningful.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot element `MedicationDispense.context`: max 1, Reference(Encounter|EpisodeOfCare), definition says encounter or episode of care establishes context.
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot element `MedicationDispense.encounter`: max 1, Reference(Encounter), definition says the encounter establishes context.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 / trial-use is neutral; it does not force preservation, but it also does not erase lossy migration for contextual clinical/administrative data.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the R4 `context` property is not the R6 path, and EpisodeOfCare references cannot be represented by the narrowed R6 target.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could keep deprecated `context` for Encounter/EpisodeOfCare or add a separate optional episode-level context while preferring `encounter`. The tradeoff is an extra contextual relationship to reconcile, but it would preserve old EpisodeOfCare data more directly.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Partially agree with the existing medium-impact finding, but the fresh review is less convinced that the partial alternative is too costly; the EpisodeOfCare loss deserves revisit.

findings.title: MedicationDispense.detectedIssue was removed

newState.summary: R6 has no local `MedicationDispense.detectedIssue` element; DetectedIssue appears only as a possible `notPerformedReason` reference.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance carrying `detectedIssue` contains an unknown R6 element. The possible R6 DetectedIssue reference is semantically narrower.

justification.inferredGoal: Possibly consolidate issue references with non-performance reason.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The supplied computable evidence does not show an exact R6 replacement for completed-dispense or broader clinical issue links. `notPerformedReason` can reference DetectedIssue only for non-performance rationale, so removal of the optional R4 relationship appears avoidable unless an external rationale shows the broader relationship was intentionally unsafe or redundant.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `MedicationDispense.detectedIssue` at `0..*`, mark it deprecated if needed, and add `notPerformedReason` for the narrower non-performance use case. That preserves R4 safety and audit data with manageable overlap; applications can distinguish detected issues associated with the dispense from reasons the dispense was not performed.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain optional `detectedIssue` as a deprecated broad safety/audit link while adding `notPerformedReason`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps a legacy DetectedIssue relationship with some overlap, but avoids losing safety-relevant issue links.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 could attach detected clinical issues to the dispense; R6 removed that local surface.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Completed dispenses with safety issues cannot be mapped to `notPerformedReason` without changing meaning.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify each DetectedIssue. Use `notPerformedReason` only when it explains non-performance; otherwise use extension/profile/external linkage and report data loss.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This removal appears avoidable from computable evidence because retaining an optional deprecated element would preserve old data.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed repeatable `detectedIssue` references for actual or potential clinical issues associated with the dispense, including actions taken to address them. R6 removes that local path; `notPerformedReason` can reference DetectedIssue only for the narrower case where the dispense was not performed. Completed or otherwise performed dispenses with safety issues therefore lose a direct base representation. Because the removed path is optional and safety/audit relevant, retaining it as deprecated would have been a plausible, modest base-compatible design.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot element `MedicationDispense.detectedIssue`: max *, Reference(DetectedIssue), definition covers actual or potential clinical issues and actions taken.
No R6 snapshot element `MedicationDispense.detectedIssue` is present.
R6 `MedicationDispense.notPerformedReason` references DetectedIssue only as the reason why a dispense was not performed.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 / trial-use is neutral, but the path carries medication safety and audit meaning when used, so the removal should not be dismissed as low-stability churn.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances carrying `detectedIssue` contain an unknown R6 element, and broader performed-dispense issue links have no direct R6 base home.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could keep `detectedIssue` at 0..* as a deprecated broad safety/audit link while adding `notPerformedReason` for non-performance. The tradeoff is some overlap, but the semantics are distinguishable and the preservation value is high.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing medium-impact and less-breaking-alternative assessment; this removal warrants revisit.

findings.title: dosageInstruction changed from repeating Dosage array to singleton DosageDetails

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 JSON uses an array of Dosage; R6 expects a singleton DosageDetails object. Multiple old instructions require clinical merge policy, and R6 DosageDetails can express staged details not cleanly representable as R4 repeats.

justification.inferredGoal: Move to richer DosageDetails course modeling.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving to `DosageDetails` is a substantial modeling change that can represent a rendered course and structured steps, so the goal is reasonable. The less-breaking alternative would preserve old data, but dosage instructions are safety-critical and duplicate same-resource dosage models could conflict, so the breaking normalization is probably justified though not proven by an official rationale.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative could retain the R4 repeating `Dosage` element and add a new optional `DosageDetails` element for richer R6 courses. This would cover common R4 instances and avoid the array-to-object break, but implementers would need rules for whether Dosage or DosageDetails controls when both are present, how to merge multiple Dosage entries into one rendered course, and how to prevent deprecated dosage representations from persisting indefinitely.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain repeating R4 `dosageInstruction` Dosage during transition and add a separate DosageDetails representation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old dosage arrays, but creates duplicate clinically sensitive dosage models with merge and precedence ambiguity.

findings.narrativeMd: `dosageInstruction` changed cardinality and datatype. This breaks even a single old array representation and is clinically sensitive for multiple/tapering instructions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 arrays are invalid as R6 singleton objects; multiple instructions cannot be losslessly placed into the R6 base element without restructuring.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build a dosage-specific converter; simple text can populate `DosageDetails.renderedInstruction`, while complex or multiple instructions need clinical/manual review and tests.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer model may be justified, but preserving old repeated Dosage during transition would reduce risk.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `dosageInstruction` changed from repeatable R4 `Dosage` to a singleton R6 `DosageDetails`. This breaks raw R4 arrays and forces a dosage-aware transform; multiple R4 instructions or structured instructions without rendered text may need clinical review because R6 DosageDetails requires a complete rendered instruction. The burden is significant and safety-sensitive, but the R6 goal is also safety-relevant: represent the full dosage course in one richer structure. Keeping old repeating Dosage alongside DosageDetails would create duplicate, potentially conflicting dosage representations.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot element `MedicationDispense.dosageInstruction`: max *, type Dosage.
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot element `MedicationDispense.dosageInstruction`: max 1, type DosageDetails.
R6 DosageDetails snapshot element `DosageDetails.renderedInstruction`: min 1, max 1, required full representation of the dosage instructions.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2 / trial-use is neutral. The high practical concern comes from dosage safety and expert-dependent conversion, not from normative maturity.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 array-of-Dosage shape is not the R6 singleton DosageDetails shape; R6-to-R4 loss can occur for DosageDetails content that has no direct R4 Dosage equivalent.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial alternative could retain repeatable Dosage during transition and add a separate DosageDetails element. That would preserve old data, but it would duplicate clinically sensitive dosage models and require precedence, merge, and conflict handling when both are present.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing high-impact and partial-alternative assessment; this is a serious migration issue but the less-breaking base alternatives have material safety tradeoffs.

findings.title: substitution.responsibleParty changed from repeating to singleton and added Organization target

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old arrays and multiple parties need conversion; R6 Organization references are outside the R4 target list.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent one primary substitution responsible party and allow organization-level responsibility.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding Organization is a reasonable expressiveness improvement and could have been done without reducing cardinality. The R4 definition already described primary responsibility despite repeatability, so the supplied evidence does not show that invalidating multiple responsible parties was necessary in the base resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `responsibleParty` repeatable, add Organization to the target list, and clarify that profiles or business rules should identify a single primary party when required. This preserves all R4 instances and meets the organization-responsibility goal; the tradeoff is continued ambiguity for uncommon cases with multiple parties, but that is a moderate interoperability cost rather than an unavoidable base break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add Organization as a target while retaining max `*`, with profiles or guidance for single-primary use cases.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves rare multi-party R4 data, but weakens base enforcement that exactly one party has primary substitution responsibility.

findings.narrativeMd: The substitution responsible party is no longer repeatable.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 multiple responsible parties cannot fit R6 without selecting one; R6 Organization cannot validate in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Choose a primary party by policy and preserve others or Organization references with extensions/audit linkage.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The max reduction was avoidable if the goal was only to add Organization.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `substitution.responsibleParty` changed from repeatable Practitioner/PractitionerRole references to a singleton that also permits Organization. Adding Organization is reasonable, but reducing max from `*` to `1` invalidates old records with multiple responsible parties and forces a policy decision about which party to keep. Since R4 already described primary responsibility despite repeatability, the max reduction appears avoidable in the base resource.

freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with multiple responsible parties exceed the R6 max; R6-to-R4 loss also occurs for Organization references.

freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing medium-impact and less-breaking-alternative assessment; the cardinality reduction should be revisited.
